title: India, 1900
tagline: Famine relief, plague vaccine and a railway of 25,400 miles.

locale.persona: a household in a town or village of British India (typical, not one named family)
locale.placeNameNote: Period place names with today's name in brackets on first mention, e.g. Bombay (now Mumbai).

morningRoutine.detail: For most working families fuel meant sticks and cow-dung; the Gazetteer notes a labourer's hut and scanty clothing cost him little and that food was by far his chief expense.

source.label: The Imperial Gazetteer of India, The Indian Empire, vol. III: Economic (1907), Oxford, Clarendon Press, ch. IX 'Rents, Prices, and Wages', via the Internet Archive

morningRoutine.detail: In Bengal and Assam the staple food was rice, the grain whose price the Gazetteer says had risen more than that of any other food-grain since 1873.

source.label: The Imperial Gazetteer of India, The Indian Empire, vol. III: Economic (1907), Oxford, Clarendon Press, ch. IX 'Rents, Prices, and Wages', via the Internet Archive

morningRoutine.detail: Many farm labourers were paid wholly or partly in grain, with perhaps a free meal or a cash wage near towns; casual workers might be idle three or four months of the year.

source.label: The Imperial Gazetteer of India, The Indian Empire, vol. III: Economic (1907), Oxford, Clarendon Press, ch. IX 'Rents, Prices, and Wages', via the Internet Archive

morningRoutine.activity: A money order from the post office
morningRoutine.detail: The post office issued 12,922,465 inland money orders in 1900-01, worth about Rs 26 crore, up from 7.3 million ten years earlier.

source.label: The Imperial Gazetteer of India, The Indian Empire, vol. III: Economic (1907), Oxford, Clarendon Press, via the Internet Archive

technology.name: Haffkine's plague vaccine
technology.description: Waldemar Haffkine tested his plague vaccine on himself in Bombay in January 1897. By the turn of the century about four million people in India had received it.

source.label: Wikipedia: Waldemar Haffkine

technology.name: Bose's millimetre radio waves
technology.description: In Calcutta in 1895 Jagadish Chandra Bose rang a bell and fired gunpowder from across a room with millimetre-wavelength waves. In 1900 he presented his research at the International Congress of Physics in Paris.

source.label: Wikipedia: Jagadish Chandra Bose
